Chapter 4

Metrics

What you measure is what you get. A metric is a contract between the model and the business — pick the wrong one and the optimizer will find the most efficient way to fail your actual goal.

4.1 Classification, dissected

Every classification evaluation starts from the confusion matrix: TP true positives, FP false positives, TN true negatives, FN false negatives. From those four cells:

accuracy = (TP + TN) / N             # overall correctness — useless when classes are rare
precision =  TP / (TP + FP)          # of what you flagged, how much was real? (cost of false alarms)
recall     =  TP / (TP + FN)         # of what was real, how much did you catch? (cost of misses)
F1         =  2·P·R / (P + R)        # harmonic mean — punishes lopsidedness
Fβ         =  (1+β²)·P·R / (β²·P + R) # β>1 weights recall; β<1 weights precision

On an imbalanced dataset (fraud: 0.2% positive), a model that flags nothing scores 99.8% accuracy and catches nothing. Recall and precision are the honest currencies; F1 and Fβ let you encode the trade-off numerically — F2 says "missing cases hurt twice as much as false alarms."

ScenarioPriorityLead metric
Fraud / spam detectionDon't miss real fraud; false alarms tolerableRecall at fixed precision, PR-AUC
Medical screeningMissing disease is catastrophicSensitivity (recall) at high specificity
Ad click predictionFlags must be trustworthyPrecision, top-k lift
Balanced multiclassEven performance across classesMacro-averaged F1
Rare-class multiclassDon't let the majority drown the minorityWeighted F1 / per-class recall report

4.2 Ranking: ROC and PR curves

Real classifiers emit probabilities, and a threshold is a business decision — so evaluate the whole curve, not one cut point. ROC-AUC plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate across all thresholds; it measures the probability that a random positive ranks above a random negative. Under extreme imbalance it looks flattering, because the FPR denominator is huge. PR-AUC plots precision against recall and is the correct lens when positives are rare — it answers "when I flag this many, how many are real?"

  • Use ROC-AUC when classes are reasonably balanced and you need a threshold-free summary. AUC = 0.5 is a coin; 0.9+ is strong; report the confidence interval, not just the point.
  • Use PR-AUC when positives are rare (under ~5%) or the cost asymmetry is extreme. A model can post great ROC-AUC and still be practically useless at the operating point you deploy at.

4.3 Regression metrics

MetricFormula / ideaBest for
MSEmean((y−ŷ)²)Default differentiable loss; punishes large errors hard
RMSE√MSEReporting in target units; same penalty profile as MSE
MAEmean(|y−ŷ|)Robustness to outliers; straight-line interpretation
HuberMSE near zero, MAE in the tailsNoisy labels — MSE's gradient with MAE's robustness
Quantile lossAsymmetric penalty per quantile τPrediction intervals, "95th percentile of delivery time"

Always pair a point metric with an error distribution: mean error (bias), a histogram of residuals, and a Q–Q plot. A model with zero mean error can still be systematically wrong in the tails, where the money is.

4.4 Language and generation metrics

  • Perplexity — exp(−log-likelihood); the model's effective branching factor. Excellent for tracking pretraining health; weak as a proxy for task quality.
  • BLEU / ROUGE — n-gram overlap with references. Fast and cheap, but they reward fluent generic text over correct specific text. Use for regression monitoring, not go/no-go decisions.
  • BERTScore — embedding similarity between generated and reference tokens. More tolerant of paraphrase; still reference-bound.
  • LLM-as-judge — a strong model grades outputs against a rubric. The current standard for open-ended quality, with real caveats: self-preference bias, positional bias, and rubric drift. Calibrate against human scores on a held-out set.
  • Task metrics — for grounded tasks (code, math, extraction), prefer execution pass rate, exact set match, or schema validation. Verifiable beats vibes.

4.5 Fairness and calibration

A global metric can hide a failing subgroup. Report your lead metric per slice — by demographic group, region, device, or traffic source — and set launch gates on the worst slice, not the mean. Complement this with calibration: if the model says 80%, do 80% of those cases actually occur? A reliability diagram (predicted probability vs. observed frequency) exposes overconfidence; temperature scaling and isotonic regression fix it post-hoc at near-zero cost.

4.6 Feeling the precision–recall trade-off

Imagine a fraud detector facing 900 true frauds among 99,100 legitimate transactions (0.9% positive rate). The table below sweeps the decision threshold over a synthetic score distribution and shows what "better" actually means when the classes are lopsided:

ThresholdRecallPrecisionCatches (TP)False alarms (FP)F1
0.3090.9%1.6%81849,5500.032
0.4082.1%2.4%73930,5720.046
0.5069.1%3.8%62215,7270.072
0.6053.3%6.8%4806,6200.120
0.7036.9%12.8%3322,2550.190
0.8022.7%24.9%2046150.237
0.9012.2%45.1%1101340.192
  • The left side (t ≤ 0.40) is maximum recall: you catch most fraud, but the false-alarm column is the story — at 0.30 you flag 49,550 clean transactions to stop 818 frauds.
  • The middle (0.50–0.70) is where operating decisions actually happen: recall falls from about 69% to 37%, while precision climbs from 4% to 13%.
  • The right side (t ≥ 0.80) buys trust at the price of coverage: at 0.90 a flagged case is real 45% of the time, yet you still miss 88% of fraud.

No single threshold wins; the right one is defined by your cost function — the price of a missed fraud versus the price of a wrongly flagged customer. (Numbers derive from synthetic score distributions — positives ≈ N(0.62, 0.24), negatives ≈ N(0.30, 0.20). The shape is the point, not the digits.)

Chapter 5

Training Methods

Optimization: walking a mountain range in the dark. The loss surface of a modern network is non-convex, wildly scaled, and studded with saddle points — training is the art of still finding a good valley.

5.1 Gradient descent and its descendants

Batch GD computes the exact gradient per step — accurate, but memory-heavy. SGD uses one sample — noisy, but the noise is a feature: it escapes sharp minima. Mini-batch SGD is the practical middle. Modern optimizers stack clever state on top of SGD:

OptimizerIdeaWhen to reach for it
MomentumAccumulates a velocity term; smooths oscillationsDefault upgrade over vanilla SGD for deep nets
AdaGradPer-parameter adaptive LR from accumulated gradientsSparse features (early NLP); LR decays too aggressively for dense nets
RMSPropExponentially-decayed adaptive LRFixes AdaGrad's decay; classic for RNNs
AdamMomentum + RMSProp (1st and 2nd moment estimates)The workhorse default; fast, forgiving hyperparameters
AdamWAdam with decoupled weight decayTransformers and large-scale training; the modern default
SGD + momentumThe classic, tuned carefullyOften edges out Adam on final accuracy for CV tasks if you have the tuning budget

5.2 Learning rate: the number that matters most

No hyperparameter changes outcomes as much as the learning rate. Too high and the loss diverges or oscillates forever; too low and you crawl. The modern playbook:

  • LR range test. Sweep log-spaced LRs for a few hundred steps; pick the highest rate whose loss is still descending — the "no-divergence point," often a hair below the minimum observed loss.
  • Warmup. Start small (1–5% of peak) and ramp linearly; stabilizes early training while normalization statistics are still settling.
  • Scheduled decay. Cosine annealing to a low floor is the transformer standard; step decay remains common in CV.
  • Batch-size coupling. Larger batches permit higher LRs (linear scaling rule), but reduce the beneficial noise — watch generalization.
  • Gradient clipping. Clip the global norm (typically to 1.0); cheap insurance against explosion, especially in RNNs and early transformer layers.

5.3 Regularization: the anti-overfit toolkit

TechniqueWhat it doesWhen to use it
AugmentationCrops, flips, color jitter, MixUp, cutmix; synonym dropout for text; controlled noise for tablesThe strongest regularizer in vision — if the validation gap is your problem, augment harder before touching the model
Weight decay and dropoutDecoupled L2 shrinks weights and smooths the landscape; dropout mutes units each step, forcing redundancyBoth cheap, both effective, both worth tuning — don't leave them at defaults forever
Early stopping and ensemblingStop when validation loss plateaus (free regularization with built-in model selection); ensemble seeds or architecturesEnsembling is the highest-leverage "last 2%" before you ship
Architectural and data-basedSmaller capacity, depthwise separable convs, distillation from a big teacher into a small studentAnd the quiet giant: more, better data beats most regularization tricks — spend there first

5.4 Diagnosing the two classic failures

Underfitting — the model is too weak

Train and validation loss are both high and still descending: the model hasn't learned the structure. Fixes: more capacity, better features, longer training, a higher learning rate. Check for bugs first — a loss that can't move is often a dead activation or a forgotten optimizer.step().

Overfitting — the model is memorizing

Train loss keeps falling while validation loss turns upward: the model is fitting noise. Fixes: more data, augmentation, dropout, weight decay, early stopping, a smaller model. If the gap is huge, suspect label noise or leakage before anything else.

5.5 Pretraining and fine-tuning

The modern training stack is layered. Pretraining learns general representations from massive unlabeled (or self-supervised) data — next-token prediction for text, masked modeling for encoders, denoising for diffusion. Fine-tuning adapts those weights to your task with far less data. Parameter-efficient variants — LoRA (low-rank adapters), prefix tuning, adapters — update a small fraction of the weights and make large-model adaptation practical on a single GPU. The rule of thumb: freeze the backbone, tune the head, add LoRA only when you need the capacity. And RLHF / DPO layers preference learning on top — for behavior, not just accuracy.

5.6 Scaling, hardware, and the practicalities of big training

  • Mixed precision (FP16 / BF16). Halves memory and roughly doubles throughput; BF16 is the safe default for large transformers, with loss scaling for FP16.
  • Gradient accumulation. Simulate a larger batch when the GPU can't hold one; mathematically equivalent (modulo batch-norm nuances).
  • Distributed strategies. Data parallelism (shard batches), tensor parallelism (shard layers), pipeline parallelism (shard stages), and ZeRO / FSDP (shard optimizer state and parameters). Choose by where your memory bottleneck is.
  • Checkpointing and fault tolerance. At scale, hardware will fail mid-run. Async checkpoints, elastic re-launch, and deterministic replay are part of the architecture, not an afterthought.
  • Scaling laws. Loss scales as a power law in model size, dataset size, and compute (Chinchilla: match tokens to parameters at roughly 20:1). Use them to decide the shape of your budget before you spend it.
  • Reproducibility. Pin seeds, log everything (W&B / MLflow), version data and code. A run you can't reproduce is a run you can't defend.

Chapter 6

Beyond Training

A model isn't finished when it trains. It's finished when it's trusted. The final mile is where most projects actually die — not in the loss curve, but in the deployment, the drift, the stakeholder meeting, and the 2 a.m. incident.

6.1 Evaluation and model selection

Lock the test set. Run the full metric suite — lead metric, slices, calibration, latency, cost. Select the checkpoint by validation performance only, then report the test set once. If you look at the test set repeatedly, it becomes validation; that's why careful teams keep a "gold" set that is scored exactly twice, ever. Define the launch gates before the run, not after.

6.2 Optimization and packaging

Export to ONNX or a runtime format, quantize (INT8 / INT4) where accuracy holds, prune or distill if the serving budget is tight, and bake the preprocessing into the artifact. The model and its transforms ship as one unit — a model file without its scaler is a promise without a contract.

6.3 Serving and inference

Choose the topology: REST for simple requests, streaming for generation, batch for offline scoring. Batch aggressively — GPU utilization scales with batch size until latency dies. Set timeouts, rate limits, and a graceful fallback (cached answer, smaller model, human queue) for when the fast path fails.

6.4 Monitoring and drift

Track three families of signals: input drift (feature distributions vs. training), prediction drift (score distribution over time), and outcome drift (do labels still arrive, and does the model still predict them well?). Alert on PSI or KL divergence per feature; retraining triggers should be defined in advance, not invented in the incident channel.

6.5 Retraining and lifecycle

Schedule retraining on data freshness, not calendar convenience. Version every artifact — model, data, code, config — as a single deployable unit. Keep the last known-good checkpoint hot for instant rollback, and automate the champion/challenger comparison so a new model must beat the old one on the live eval set before it earns production.

6.6 Governance and continuous audit

Maintain the model card: intended use, known limitations, slice performance, and a named rollback owner. Run periodic fairness and safety audits, especially after any data or model change. Treat the model as a regulated surface — the same review rigor you'd give a payment system, scaled to its actual blast radius.

The MLOps loop, in one sentence

Capture → curate → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor → detect drift → re-capture. The loop, not the model, is the product.

05 · Training MethodsOptimizers · learning-rate strategy · regularization · under/overfit diagnosis · pretraining and fine-tuning · scaling laws~60 min
06 · Beyond TrainingEvaluation discipline · packaging and serving · drift monitoring · retraining lifecycle · governance~40 min
07 · PracticeSix hands-on exercises woven through the modules — from logistic regression to a load-tested, monitored endpointongoing

7.1 Where to go from here

The canonical texts

Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville's Deep Learning is the mathematical spine; Caruana and colleagues' Practical Tips for Predicting Real-World Distributions collects the field's hard-won heuristics; Attention Is All You Need is the fifteen pages that reshaped the decade. Read the paper, then re-read it after building one.

The hands-on path

Rebuild each architecture from scratch in NumPy before using a framework. Then in PyTorch. Then at scale. The gaps between those three versions are where the real learning lives.

The career path

Ship one small model end-to-end — data, metric, deployment, monitoring — before chasing frontier research. Production scars teach what no paper can: what breaks, when, and why.

The last line of the course

The model is never finished; the work is. Data shifts, users adapt, and the metric that mattered in Q1 is stale by Q3. The practitioners who last aren't the ones who train the biggest model — they're the ones who run the loop honestly, measure what they claim, and ship what they can defend.

Glossary

Backpropagation
Application of the chain rule that computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter in a single backward pass.
Batch size
The number of examples processed per optimizer step; interacts with learning rate, memory, and generalization.
Causal masking
The decoder-only trick of letting a position attend only to earlier positions, making next-token prediction well-defined.
Class imbalance
One label far rarer than the others, making accuracy misleading and precision/recall the honest metrics.
Data leakage
Information from validation/test (or the future) sneaking into training and inflating scores; the most common silent failure.
Drift
Live data distributions shifting away from training distributions, quietly degrading performance.
Embedding
A learned dense vector representation of a discrete item — a word, a user, an image patch.
Epoch
One full pass over the training data.
Fine-tuning
Adapting pretrained weights to a task with far less data.
Gradient
The direction of steepest ascent of the loss; optimizers step against it.
Inference
Running a trained model on new inputs — the latency and cost stage.
Overfitting
Fitting noise: training error falls while validation error rises.
Perplexity
exp(−average log-likelihood); a language model's effective branching factor.
Regularization
Any constraint that fights overfitting: weight decay, dropout, augmentation, early stopping, capacity limits.
Residual connection
A skip link, y = F(x) + x, that lets gradients flow through deep networks.
Warmup
The short opening phase of training in which the learning rate ramps up from a small value.

Further Study

Books

  • Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville — Deep Learning. The mathematical spine of the field.
  • Aurélien Géron — Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras & TensorFlow. Practical momentum for every chapter of this book.
  • Caruana, Niculescu-Miziel, Crew, Kirsch — Practical Tips for Predicting Real-World Distributions. Working paper, but the field's best collection of heuristics.

Papers

  • Vaswani et al. (2017) — Attention Is All You Need. The transformer, in fifteen pages.
  • Devlin et al. (2018) — BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers. Encoder-side pretraining.
  • Hu et al. (2021) — LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
  • Hoffmann et al. (2022) — Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models. Scaling laws (Chinchilla).

Practice

  • Rebuild each architecture in this book in three fidelities: NumPy, PyTorch, at scale. The gaps between the versions are the course.
  • Ship one model end-to-end — data, metric, deployment, monitoring — before reading the next paper.

Colophon

Curriculum — A Field Course in Creating AI Models

Set in Georgia and system monospace. Compiled as a single HTML file, Tome.html — the web edition lives in Curriculum.html.

EPUB edition built by make_epub.py · Conversion instructions in README.md.

Seven chapters · Six exercises · Single-file edition, 2025.

Freely reusable and redistributable — cite it, convert it, teach it.

files.README.md:
# Curriculum — Ebook & Conversion Guide

This folder contains the full course as an ebook plus the tooling to ship it in
every major ebook format:

| File            | What it is                                                            |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tome.html`     | The complete ebook in one book-styled file. Open it in any browser.   |
| `make_epub.py`  | Zero-dependency Python script that compiles `Tome.html` → real EPUB 3 |
| `README.md`     | This guide — how to build EPUB and MOBI                               |

The ebook mirrors the webpage course: 7 chapters (Foundations, Architectures,
Data, Metrics, Training, Beyond Training, Practice) plus preface, glossary,
further-study, and colophon — with a clickable table of contents.

---

## 1) Build the EPUB (no installs required)

Requires **Python 3.8+** (standard library only — no pip packages).

```bash
python3 make_epub.py
# → builds Tome.epub

# custom output name:
python3 make_epub.py --out MyBook.epub

# build from a modified copy of the ebook:
python3 make_epub.py --source Tome.html --out Edition2.epub
```

The script:

1. extracts the book's stylesheet into `style.css`,
2. splits the HTML at its `<!-- PART:... -->` markers into one XHTML file per
   chapter,
3. writes a spec-compliant EPUB 3 package (`mimetype` stored first, OPF
   manifest/spine, EPUB 3 `nav` **and** legacy NCX, so both modern and older
   readers get a working, clickable table of contents).

Validate the result (optional):

- **Calibre**: *Tools → Check book* → select `Tome.epub`.
- **Online**: <https://validate.idpf.org> (W3C EPUB validator).
- **Quick test**: open it in Apple Books, Kobo, or the free [Calibre E-book Viewer](https://calibre-ebook.com).

## 2) Convert EPUB → MOBI (Kindle)

> Note: Amazon has been migrating Kindle to **KFX** and continues to accept
> **EPUB** directly in many places (including Kindle Personal Document email
> and "Send to Kindle"), so EPUB is often the safest upload. MOBI is still
> supported by the Calibre/Kindle pipeline below.

**Option A — Calibre (recommended, free, cross-platform)**

1. Install [Calibre](https://calibre-ebook.com).
2. Double-click `Tome.epub` to add it to the library (or *Add books*).
3. Select it → **Convert books** (or press `K`).
4. In the *Output format* dropdown, choose **MOBI** (or **AZW3** for newer
   Kindles, which renders the layout better).
5. (Optional) Metadata tab: set title, author, language.
6. *OK* → find `Tome.mobi` in your Calibre library folder.

**Option B — Calibre Command Line (calibre-ebook-convert)**

```bash
# after installing Calibre (its CLI is on PATH on most systems):
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub Tome.mobi
# or, for better rendering on modern Kindles:
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub Tome.azw3
```

Useful flags:

```bash
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub Tome.mobi \
  --title "Curriculum: A Field Course in Creating AI Models" \
  --author "Field Course Press" \
  --language en
```

**Option C — Send to Kindle (no MOBI at all)**

Email the `.epub` to your registered `name@kindle.com` address (from a
whitelisted sender), or drag it onto the *Send to Kindle* web app.

## 3) Other formats (Calibre converts all of these)

```bash
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub Tome.pdf      # print-friendly
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub Tome.epub     # (identity, e.g. to re-zip)
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub book.fb2      # FB2
calibre-ebook-convert Tome.epub book.kepub    # Kobo
```

Or use the GUI: select the book → *Convert books* → pick any output format.

## 4) Read it right now

`Tome.html` opens directly in any browser — no build step, no network needed
(it uses system serif and monospace fonts). The Contents page links jump to
each chapter in the browser, and become the reader's clickable table of
contents once converted to EPUB. Print it too: the file carries dedicated
print styles with per-chapter page breaks.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                              | Fix                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `python3` not found                  | Install Python 3 from <https://python.org>, or use `py make_epub.py` on Windows |
| Validator complains about `mimetype` | Use the EPUB produced by `make_epub.py` (it stores `mimetype` first, uncompressed) |
| TOC not clickable in a very old reader | The package includes both EPUB 3 `nav` **and** NCX; if a reader still ignores it, re-convert through Calibre (it rewrites metadata) |
| MOBI looks cramped                   | Prefer AZW3, or in Calibre's conversion set *Output lookup → MOBI → MOBI options* and enable "Enable MOBI output for Kindle devices" |
| Changed the text, want a new build   | Just re-run `python3 make_epub.py` — it reads `Tome.html` fresh each time |

---

*Curriculum · Cohort 2025 — one HTML file, one Python script, every major ebook format.*

  position:absolute;top:3px;left:3px;width:22px;height:22px;border-radius:50%;
  background:var(--accent);color:var(--accent-ink);display:grid;place-items:center;
  transition:transform .45s cubic-bezier(.6,-.28,.3,1.3),background .4s;
}
.toggle .knob svg{width:13px;height:13px;stroke:currentColor;fill:none;stroke-width:2;stroke-linecap:round}
.toggle .knob .sun{display:none}
:root[data-theme="light"] .toggle .knob{transform:translateX(32px)}
:root[data-theme="light"] .toggle .knob .moon{display:none}
:root[data-theme="light"] .toggle .knob .sun{display:block}
.toggle:hover{border-color:var(--accent)}

/* ============================================================ rail */
.rail{
  position:fixed;top:var(--topbar-h);bottom:0;left:0;width:var(--rail);z-index:100;
  border-right:1px solid var(--line-soft);
  display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:4px;
  padding:20px 0;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--bg) 60%,transparent);
}
.rail a{
  width:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:5px;
  padding:10px 0;color:var(--ink-mute);transition:color .3s;position:relative;
}
.rail a .rnum{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px}
.rail a .rbar{width:22px;height:2px;background:currentColor;opacity:.35;transition:all .35s}
.rail a:hover{color:var(--ink)}
.rail a.active{color:var(--accent)}
.rail a.active .rbar{width:34px;opacity:1}

/* ============================================================ layout */
main{margin-left:var(--rail);padding-top:var(--topbar-h)}
.wrap{max-width:var(--max);margin:0 auto;padding:0 clamp(20px,4.5vw,56px)}
.chapter{padding:clamp(70px,9vw,120px) 0;position:relative}
.chapter:nth-child(even){background:var(--bg-2);transition:background .5s ease}
.chapter-head{max-width:820px;margin-bottom:clamp(40px,5vw,64px)}
.kicker{
  display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:.28em;text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:20px;
}
.kicker::before{content:"";width:34px;height:1px;background:var(--accent)}
.chapter h2{font-size:clamp(2.1rem,4.6vw,3.4rem);font-weight:600}
.chapter h2 em{font-style:italic;font-weight:500;color:var(--ink-soft)}
.chapter .lede{margin-top:18px;font-size:clamp(1.05rem,1.6vw,1.2rem);color:var(--ink-soft);max-width:660px}
.chapter .lede strong{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}
h3{font-size:clamp(1.35rem,2.2vw,1.7rem);margin-bottom:14px}
h3 .hn{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:.72em;color:var(--accent);margin-right:10px;letter-spacing:.08em;vertical-align:2px}
p{margin-bottom:1em;color:var(--ink-soft)}
p strong,li strong{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}
ul.dash{list-style:none;margin:0 0 1.2em}
ul.dash li{position:relative;padding-left:26px;margin-bottom:.55em;color:var(--ink-soft)}
ul.dash li::before{content:"—";position:absolute;left:0;color:var(--accent);font-family:var(--font-mono)}
.subblock{margin:56px 0}

/* reveal-on-scroll */
.rv{opacity:0;transform:translateY(26px);transition:opacity .8s ease,transform .8s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1);transition-delay:var(--d,0s)}
.rv.on{opacity:1;transform:none}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){
  .rv{opacity:1;transform:none;transition:none}
  .brand-mark::after{animation:none}
  html{scroll-behavior:auto}
}

/* ============================================================ cards & grids */
.card{
  background:var(--bg);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;
  padding:26px 26px 22px;position:relative;transition:transform .35s ease,border-color .35s ease,box-shadow .35s ease;
  height:100%;
}
:root[data-theme="light"] .chapter:nth-child(even) .card{background:var(--bg)}
.card::before{
  content:attr(data-glyph);position:absolute;top:-14px;left:20px;
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.18em;
  background:var(--bg-2);padding:2px 10px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:99px;color:var(--ink-mute);
}
.chapter:nth-child(even) .card::before{background:var(--bg-2)}
.card:hover{transform:translateY(-6px);border-color:var(--accent);box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.card h4{font-size:1.22rem;margin-bottom:8px}
.card .ctag{display:block;font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.14em;color:var(--accent-2);text-transform:uppercase;margin-bottom:10px}
.card p{font-size:.95rem;margin:0}
.grid{display:grid;gap:20px}
.grid.c2{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}
.grid.c3{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)}
.grid.c4{grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)}
@media (max-width:980px){.grid.c4{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}.grid.c3{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}}
@media (max-width:640px){.grid.c2,.grid.c3,.grid.c4{grid-template-columns:1fr}.card::before{display:none}}

/* callouts */
.callout{
  border-left:3px solid var(--accent);background:var(--chip);
  border-radius:0 12px 12px 0;padding:18px 22px;margin:30px 0;
}
.callout .ct{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.22em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent);display:block;margin-bottom:8px}
.callout p{margin:0;font-size:.98rem}
.callout.key{border-left-color:var(--accent-2)}
.callout.key .ct{color:var(--accent-2)}

/* tables */
.tbl-wrap{overflow-x:auto;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;margin:26px 0;background:var(--bg)}
:root[data-theme="light"] .chapter:nth-child(even) .tbl-wrap{background:var(--bg)}
table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.93rem;min-width:640px}
th{
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;
  text-align:left;color:var(--ink-mute);padding:13px 18px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);
  background:var(--chip);white-space:nowrap;
}
td{padding:13px 18px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft);color:var(--ink-soft);vertical-align:top}
tr:last-child td{border-bottom:none}
tbody tr{transition:background .25s}
tbody tr:hover{background:var(--chip)}
td b{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}

/* code */
pre{
  background:var(--code-bg);color:var(--code-ink);border:1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius:12px;padding:22px 24px;overflow-x:auto;margin:24px 0;
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:.86rem;line-height:1.75;
}
code{font-family:var(--font-mono)}
p code,li code,td code{
  font-size:.85em;background:var(--chip);border:1px solid var(--line-soft);
  padding:.1em .45em;border-radius:5px;color:var(--accent);white-space:nowrap;
}
pre .cm{color:#7d8aa0}
pre .kw{color:#e8b25a}
pre .st{color:#8fd6b4}
pre .fn{color:#7cc7d4}

/* exercises */
.exercise{
  margin:34px 0;border:1px dashed var(--accent);border-radius:14px;padding:24px 26px;position:relative;
  background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 5%,transparent);
}
.exercise .etag{
  position:absolute;top:-12px;left:20px;background:var(--accent);color:var(--accent-ink);
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.2em;text-transform:uppercase;
  padding:4px 12px;border-radius:99px;font-weight:600;
}
.exercise ol{padding-left:20px;margin:10px 0 0}
.exercise li{margin-bottom:.5em;color:var(--ink-soft)}

/* ============================================================ HERO */
.hero{
  min-height:calc(100vh - var(--topbar-h));
  display:flex;align-items:center;position:relative;overflow:hidden;
  background:
    radial-gradient(900px 500px at 85% 12%, var(--glow), transparent 60%),
    var(--bg);
  transition:background .5s ease;
}
.hero::before{
  content:"";position:absolute;inset:0;
  background-image:
    linear-gradient(var(--line-soft) 1px,transparent 1px),
    linear-gradient(90deg,var(--line-soft) 1px,transparent 1px);
  background-size:56px 56px;
  mask-image:radial-gradient(ellipse 90% 80% at 50% 40%,black 30%,transparent 75%);
  -webkit-mask-image:radial-gradient(ellipse 90% 80% at 50% 40%,black 30%,transparent 75%);
}
.hero-inner{position:relative;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.05fr .95fr;gap:clamp(30px,5vw,70px);align-items:center;width:100%;padding:70px 0}
@media (max-width:920px){.hero-inner{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.hero-tag{
  display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:99px;
  padding:7px 16px;font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.2em;text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--ink-soft);margin-bottom:26px;
}
.hero-tag i{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--accent);animation:blink 2.2s ease infinite}
@keyframes blink{50%{opacity:.3}}
.hero h1{
  font-size:clamp(2.7rem,6.4vw,5rem);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.02em;line-height:1.04;
}
.hero h1 .line{display:block;overflow:hidden}
.hero h1 .line span{display:inline-block;transform:translateY(110%);animation:rise 1s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) forwards}
.hero h1 .line:nth-child(2) span{animation-delay:.14s}
.hero h1 .line:nth-child(3) span{animation-delay:.28s}
@keyframes rise{to{transform:none}}
.hero h1 em{font-style:italic;font-weight:500;color:var(--accent)}
.hero-sub{margin:24px 0 34px;max-width:560px;color:var(--ink-soft);font-size:1.08rem}
.hero-actions{display:flex;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.btn{
  display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:14px 26px;border-radius:99px;
  font-weight:600;font-size:.95rem;border:1px solid var(--accent);transition:transform .3s,box-shadow .3s,background .3s,color .3s;
}
.btn.solid{background:var(--accent);color:var(--accent-ink)}
.btn.solid:hover{transform:translateY(-3px);box-shadow:0 14px 30px color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 35%,transparent)}
.btn.ghost{border-color:var(--line);color:var(--ink)}
.btn.ghost:hover{border-color:var(--accent);transform:translateY(-3px)}
.hero-meta{display:flex;gap:clamp(20px,3vw,44px);margin-top:44px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.hero-meta div b{display:block;font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1.7rem;font-weight:600}
.hero-meta div span{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-mute)}

/* hero viz */
.hero-viz{position:relative}
.hero-viz svg{width:100%;height:auto}
.node{fill:var(--bg-3);stroke:var(--accent);stroke-width:1.4;transition:fill .4s}
.node.hot{fill:var(--accent)}
.edge{stroke:var(--line);stroke-width:1;transition:stroke .4s,stroke-width .4s}
.edge.hot{stroke:var(--accent);stroke-width:2}
.pulse{fill:var(--accent-2);opacity:0;animation:travel 2.4s linear infinite}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.pulse{animation:none;display:none}}
@keyframes travel{
  0%{opacity:0}8%{opacity:1}80%{opacity:1}100%{opacity:0}
}
.hero-viz figcaption{
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--ink-mute);margin-top:14px;text-align:right;
}
.scroll-hint{
  position:absolute;bottom:26px;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.3em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-mute);
  display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:8px;
}
.scroll-hint::after{content:"";width:1px;height:34px;background:linear-gradient(var(--accent),transparent);animation:drip 1.8s ease infinite}
@keyframes drip{0%{transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:top}55%{transform:scaleY(1);transform-origin:top}56%{transform-origin:bottom}100%{transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:bottom}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.hero h1 .line span{transform:none;animation:none}.scroll-hint::after{animation:none}}

/* ============================================================ MODULE 1 */
.pipe{display:flex;align-items:stretch;gap:0;flex-wrap:wrap;margin:34px 0 10px}
.pipe-step{
  flex:1 1 150px;min-width:140px;padding:20px 18px;position:relative;
  border:1px solid var(--line);border-right:none;background:var(--bg);
}
.pipe-step:first-child{border-radius:12px 0 0 12px}
.pipe-step:last-child{border-right:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:0 12px 12px 0}
.pipe-step b{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.2em;color:var(--accent);display:block;margin-bottom:6px}
.pipe-step span{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1.05rem;font-weight:600;display:block;margin-bottom:4px}
.pipe-step small{color:var(--ink-mute);font-size:.82rem;line-height:1.4;display:block}
.pipe-step::after{
  content:"→";position:absolute;right:-9px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);
  z-index:2;color:var(--accent);font-size:15px;background:var(--bg);padding:2px 0;
}
.pipe-step:last-child::after{content:none}
@media (max-width:760px){
  .pipe{flex-direction:column}
  .pipe-step{border-right:1px solid var(--line);border-bottom:none;border-radius:0}
  .pipe-step:first-child{border-radius:12px 12px 0 0}
  .pipe-step:last-child{border-radius:0 0 12px 12px}
  .pipe-step::after{content:"↓";right:auto;left:50%;top:auto;bottom:-10px;transform:translateX(-50%)}
}
/* ============================================================ MODULE 2 */
.family{
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:190px 1fr;gap:0;border:1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius:14px;margin:22px 0;overflow:hidden;background:var(--bg);transition:background .4s;
}
.family .fhead{
  padding:22px;border-right:1px solid var(--line);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:6px;
  background:var(--chip);
}
.family .fhead b{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1.3rem;font-weight:600}
.family .fhead small{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent)}
.family .fbody{padding:22px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:18px}
.family .fbody h5{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-mute);margin-bottom:6px;font-weight:500}
.family .fbody p{font-size:.92rem;margin:0}
@media (max-width:820px){
  .family{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .family .fhead{border-right:none;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);flex-direction:row;align-items:baseline;gap:12px}
  .family .fbody{grid-template-columns:1fr}
}
.stack{margin:30px 0}
.layer{
  display:flex;align-items:center;gap:18px;border:1px solid var(--line);
  padding:16px 22px;margin-bottom:8px;background:var(--bg);transition:transform .3s,border-color .3s;
}
.layer:hover{transform:translateX(8px);border-color:var(--accent)}
.layer .lname{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.14em;width:130px;flex:none;color:var(--accent);text-transform:uppercase}
.layer .ldesc{font-size:.94rem;color:var(--ink-soft)}
.stack-arrow{text-align:center;color:var(--ink-mute);font-size:12px;margin:2px 0 10px;font-family:var(--font-mono)}
@media (max-width:560px){.layer{flex-direction:column;align-items:flex-start;gap:6px}}

/* transformer diagram */
.tf-fig{
  border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;padding:26px;margin:28px 0;
  background:
    repeating-linear-gradient(0deg,transparent 0 34px,var(--line-soft) 34px 35px),var(--bg);
}
.tf-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;margin-bottom:14px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.tf-box{
  border:1.5px solid var(--accent);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 18px;text-align:center;
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:.06em;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 8%,transparent);
  transition:transform .3s,box-shadow .3s;
}
.tf-box:hover{transform:scale(1.04);box-shadow:0 8px 22px color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 25%,transparent)}
.tf-box.alt{border-color:var(--accent-2);background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent-2) 8%,transparent)}
.tf-box b{display:block;font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1rem;letter-spacing:0;margin-bottom:2px}
.tf-arrow{color:var(--ink-mute);font-size:17px}
.tf-cap{font-size:.9rem;color:var(--ink-soft);margin:18px 0 0;max-width:700px}

/* ============================================================ MODULE 3 */
.recipe{
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 320px;gap:22px;align-items:start;
}
@media (max-width:880px){.recipe{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.steps-ol{counter-reset:st;list-style:none}
.steps-ol li{
  counter-increment:st;position:relative;padding:0 0 22px 58px;
}
.steps-ol li::before{
  content:counter(st,decimal-leading-zero);
  position:absolute;left:0;top:2px;width:38px;height:38px;border-radius:50%;
  border:1px solid var(--accent);color:var(--accent);display:grid;place-items:center;
  font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:12px;background:var(--bg);
}
.steps-ol li::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:19px;top:44px;bottom:4px;width:1px;background:var(--line)}
.steps-ol li:last-child::after{display:none}
.steps-ol b{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1.08rem;font-weight:600;display:block;margin-bottom:4px}
.steps-ol span{color:var(--ink-soft);font-size:.94rem}
.splitfig{
  border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;background:var(--bg);padding:22px;
}
.splitfig h5{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-mute);margin-bottom:14px;font-weight:500}
.bar-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:12px;font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:11px}
.bar-row .bl{width:82px;flex:none;color:var(--ink-mute)}
.bar-track{flex:1;height:20px;background:var(--chip);border-radius:6px;overflow:hidden;position:relative}
.bar-fill{height:100%;width:0;border-radius:6px;transition:width 1.2s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)}
.on .bar-fill{width:var(--w)}
.bar-fill.a{background:var(--accent)}
.bar-fill.b{background:var(--accent-2)}
.bar-row .bv{width:38px;text-align:right;color:var(--ink)}

/* ============================================================ MODULE 4 */
.gauge-card{background:var(--bg);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;padding:26px;margin:28px 0}
.gauge-svg{width:min(430px,100%);margin:0 auto;display:block}
.gauge-track{stroke:var(--line);stroke-width:14;fill:none}
.gauge-fill{stroke:var(--accent);stroke-width:14;fill:none;stroke-linecap:round;
  stroke-dasharray:409;stroke-dashoffset:409;transition:stroke-dashoffset 1.6s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)}
.gauge-center{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:2.1rem;font-weight:600;fill:var(--ink)}
.gauge-label{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.22em;fill:var(--ink-mute);text-transform:uppercase}
.gauge-controls{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:16px;margin-top:20px;max-width:460px;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto}
.gauge-controls label{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-mute);display:flex;justify-content:space-between}
.gauge-controls label output{color:var(--accent)}
input[type=range]{-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;width:100%;height:4px;border-radius:99px;background:var(--line);outline-offset:4px}
input[type=range]::-webkit-slider-thumb{
  -webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;width:18px;height:18px;border-radius:50%;
  background:var(--accent);border:3px solid var(--bg);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--accent);cursor:grab;
}
input[type=range]::-moz-range-thumb{
  width:14px;height:14px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--accent);border:3px solid var(--bg);
  box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--accent);cursor:grab;
}
.metric-note{font-size:.9rem;color:var(--ink-mute);text-align:center;font-family:var(--font-mono);margin-top:14px}

/* ============================================================ MODULE 5 */
.lost{
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:22px;margin:28px 0;
}
@media (max-width:760px){.lost{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.lost-panel{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;background:var(--bg);padding:24px;transition:transform .35s,box-shadow .35s}
.lost-panel:hover{transform:translateY(-5px);box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.lost-panel h5{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;margin-bottom:10px;font-weight:500}
.lost-panel.good h5{color:var(--ok)}
.lost-panel.bad h5{color:var(--bad)}
.lost-panel p{font-size:.94rem}
.lost-panel svg{margin-bottom:14px}
.train-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
@media (max-width:760px){.train-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}}

/* ============================================================ MODULE 6 */
.stage{
  border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;background:var(--bg);padding:26px;margin:24px 0;
  transition:border-color .4s,transform .35s;
}
.stage:hover{border-color:var(--accent);transform:translateY(-4px)}
.stage .snum{
  font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:2.6rem;font-weight:600;color:transparent;
